title: The Role of Pipe Slope in Drainage Systems
description: Gravity is the primary force moving wastewater through a residential drainage system, making proper pipe slope critical to long-term performance. If a pipe is pitched too steeply, liquid wastewater rushes past solid waste, leaving heavy particles behind to accumulate and cause clogs. Conversely, if the slope is too flat, water velocity drops below the minimum required to carry solids along the pipe bed. Maintaining correct, consistent fall ensures that both liquids and solids travel smoothly to the main sewer line. Professional installers rely on accurate measuring tools and adhere to local code specifications to establish the ideal gradient for every horizontal run.
